comment: PlayerBots. Caps are DELIBERATELY EMPTY: with no values here a bot is built to exactly the limits Config/PlayerCaps.cfg gives players, which is this shard's authoritative source and already carries the EJ values (skill 100/700, stat 125/225). Set a value only to make bots deliberately different from players - the Bots.Population health check names every override so the divergence is never silent. Destination weights multiply: byType[type][class or default] times byTag[tag][class or default] for every tag the destination carries. Absent means 1.0 (no opinion); 0 excludes. home, guard and work are excluded outright - a bot has no business loitering on a guard post, at a crier's station, or inside somebody's house. forge, mine and lumber are excluded for everyone EXCEPT the class that works them, which is how an artisan or gatherer is drawn to its own station and nobody else wanders onto a rock face. An artisan's pull now lives in its station tag (tailoring, woodworking) rather than in the generic craft tag, which before 7e was standing in for a station it did not yet have. towns lists the tags that name a town; every bot rolls one as its home at creation, weighted by how many destinations carry the tag, and a destination in the bot's home town weighs homeBias times more in every roll - uo-offline's 2.5. That is the whole of what a home does: there is no distance term for a town destination and no rule that sends a bot home, so a resident of a town with no station of its kind rolls like anyone else. Class templates, tier curves and the equipment tables live in code; see Scripts/Custom/Bots/README.md.

life.comment: phases is DELIBERATELY EMPTY: with no clamps a phase is whatever BotPersonality rolled for that bot (15-360 minutes), which is the production case. The smoke installs short clamps in memory for its own run. crowds is the standing-crowd floor per destination type - an under-floor destination pulls bots toward it rather than anyone being placed there. handoff is how often arriving somewhere turns into staying: not every arrival commits, and the ones who pass through are what make a bank look busy. station is the handoff chance used instead when a bot arrives at the station its own class works, whatever the type. capacity is the mirror of crowds and is keyed by DESTINATION ID, not type: a work site's weight falls as it fills and reaches zero at capacity, so gatherers spread across the faces instead of stacking on one. It is DELIBERATELY EMPTY - with no entry a site's capacity is its authored arrival-point count, which is the number of bots that can actually stand there.
